## Simple explanation

A yottabyte is an extremely large unit of digital information: one yottabyte
equals one septillion bytes in the decimal system.

## Technical explanation

In the International System of Units, the prefix yotta denotes $10^{24}$, so
1 YB = $10^{24}$ bytes. The binary prefix yobi denotes $2^{80}$ bytes, written
YiB, and is slightly larger. These units should not be confused in storage
capacity and data-volume calculations.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Data scale affects storage architecture, movement, retention, and compute
cost. AI practitioners are more likely to handle terabytes or petabytes, but
clear unit conventions prevent substantial estimation errors at large scale.

## How it works

Convert using powers of ten for decimal SI units (kB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB, ZB,
YB) and powers of two for IEC binary units (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB, EiB,
ZiB, YiB). State which convention a reported size uses.

## Practical example

If a data-transfer estimate uses decimal units, a sustained rate of one
terabyte per second would take about one million seconds to transfer one
yottabyte, ignoring protocol overhead and other bottlenecks.

## Common misconceptions

- Yottabyte (YB) and yobibyte (YiB) are distinct units.
- Decimal unit conversions do not describe the real time to transfer data;
  network limits and storage throughput matter.
